about: Labeled evaluation corpus for the verdict reader (product-plan 16.3). Every case is synthetic: written here by hand, modelled on verdict shapes that appear in Ursa's own trials, never copied from a private session. The one exception is 'yesss finallyyy!! lol', which is already public in product-plan 16.1, prompts/engineer-agent.md's history and src/verdict.test.ts, and is the acceptance quote the reader was built against. No case carries a home path, a macOS username, or a full session UUID (redaction rider, prompts/engineer-agent.md).

fields.id: stable case name; the harness reports per-id so a regression names itself
fields.why: the failure mode or verdict shape this case exists to hold down
fields.prompts: the UserPrompt[] handed to readVerdict, exactly the shape src/types.ts declares
fields.truth: the human label. accepted: true stated satisfaction, false stated dissatisfaction, null no stated verdict. step: the prompt that carried it, null when accepted is null. quote: the exact verbatim span the reader must return, newlines included, null when accepted is null.
fields.padding: the token PADDING_<n> inside a prompt expands, at load time, to n characters of neutral filler. It keeps a case that needs a message longer than TRANSCRIPT_CHAR_LIMIT readable in this file instead of pasting 2200 literal characters.
fields.modelReply: the exact string the injected VerdictRunner returns in replay mode. Hand-written to stand for one plausible `claude -p` reply, including the misbehaving ones; it is NOT a capture of a real model call, and replay mode therefore measures the verification layer, not the model.
fields.knownLimitation: present only when the reader provably cannot pass this case today. Counted as knownMiss, reported, and excluded from the pass/fail gate.

cases.why: the n=1's own verdict shape: exclamation, no punctuation discipline, arrives hundreds of steps in

prompts.text: make the constellation smaller and move it behind the headline
no, that is not it, try the other layout
yesss finallyyy!! lol

cases.why: the verdict message has two lines. The transcript flattens newlines to spaces before the model sees it, so the model's verbatim quote carries a space where the source carries a newline. Before 2026-09-27 the reader compared the quote against the unflattened text and discarded this true verdict as a hallucination.

truth.quote:
that is exactly it

cases.modelReply: {"accepted": true, "step": 44, "quote": "that is exactly it thank you"}

cases.why: two stated verdicts in opposite directions; the instruction says the most recent governs

cases.modelReply: {"accepted": false, "step": 18, "quote": "i was dissatisfied with that product"}

cases.why: acceptance early, dissatisfaction later, because the work kept going and got worse; the record must carry the later one

cases.modelReply: {"accepted": false, "step": 60, "quote": "this is wrong, you have buried the thing i actually cared about"}

cases.why: the commonest honest null. Every message steers the work and none evaluates it. Silence is never converted to acceptance by retention (vision 0b, the 2026-09-19 rule).

cases.why: an interrogative can sound evaluative without stating a verdict

prompts.text: is this the layout you would pick?
why did you drop the second column?

cases.why: the model invents a verdict the user never wrote. Verbatim verification is what stops it, and a false satisfied is plan 16.8 risk 1, the worst outcome in the system.

prompts.text: use the deck's accent colour, not blue
move the footer up

cases.why: the hole verbatim verification alone does not close. The model returns accepted=true quoting a word the user really did type, so presence-in-the-trace passes, but the word carries no verdict. Before 2026-09-27 this produced a false satisfied out of the word 'continue'.

prompts.text: add the health route
continue

cases.why: the cheapest hallucination shape: a quote so short it is present in almost any trace by accident and cannot carry a stated verdict

prompts.text: smaller
again

cases.why: observed in the real n=1 acceptance run: the model quoted the verdict exactly and misnumbered its step, 710 for 730. The trace is the authority, not the model's pointer.

prompts.text: no, that is not it, try the other layout
yesss finallyyy!! lol

cases.why: claude -p wraps JSON in a markdown fence often enough that a parse failure here would silently cost every label in the session

truth.quote: this is wrong, the prose is dead

cases.why: the model prefaces the object with a sentence despite being told not to; the object is still extractable and the label is still real

cases.why: zero prompts must cost zero tokens on the owner's subscription and must not produce a reading

a known limitation, measured rather than hidden. The verdict sits past TRANSCRIPT_CHAR_LIMIT inside one very long message, so the model is never shown it and the label is structurally unreachable. Counted as knownMiss; the fix (head-and-tail windowing) is a ledger entry, not this run's work.
